# Kyoto Family Trip Snapshot: 2026-04-10 to 2026-04-13

A balanced 4-day plan for **2 adults + 1 child (age 8)** with temples, food, and one kid-friendly activity each day. Budget is set to stay within **$1,800 total** excluding international flights.

## 4-Day Kyoto Itinerary and Budget Plan

### Day 1: Higashiyama Welcome Day
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- **Morning:** Kiyomizu-dera for classic Kyoto views; start early to avoid crowds.
- **Afternoon:** Walk Sannenzaka and Ninenzaka, then visit Yasaka Shrine and Gion streets.
- **Kid-friendly activity:** Tea break with a sweet stop near Higashiyama; keep the pace light after arrival.
- **Food:** Kyoto-style udon or yudofu for lunch; casual izakaya or set meal for dinner.
- **Local transport:** **¥2,000–¥3,000** total for buses/taxis and short hops.
- **Meal budget:** **¥9,000–¥12,000** total.

Action: [Button: Kiyomizu Area] https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e3931.html

### Day 2: Fushimi Inari and Central Kyoto
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg
- **Morning:** Fushimi Inari Taisha; do the lower trail section and turn back before it gets tiring for the child.
- **Afternoon:** Nishiki Market for snacks, then stroll to Teramachi/Shinkyogoku shopping arcades.
Media: Alt=Afternoon:** Nishiki Market for snacks, then stroll to Teramachi/Shinkyogoku shopping arcades, Kyoto, Japan
- **Kid-friendly activity:** Snack tasting challenge at Nishiki Market.
- **Food:** Market bites for lunch; ramen, curry rice, or tempura set for dinner.
- **Local transport:** **¥1,500–¥2,500** total, mostly train plus short walks.
- **Meal budget:** **¥10,000–¥13,000** total.

Action: [Button: Fushimi Inari] https://www.inari.jp/en/

### Day 3: Arashiyama Nature Day
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/tree.svg
- **Morning:** Arashiyama Bamboo Grove and Tenryu-ji garden.
- **Afternoon:** Togetsukyo Bridge, riverside walk, and optional monkey park if energy is good.
- **Kid-friendly activity:** Arashiyama Monkey Park Iwatayama or a short river walk with snack stops.
Media: Alt=Kid-friendly activity:** Arashiyama Monkey Park Iwatayama or a short river walk with snack stops, Kyoto, Japan
- **Food:** Tofu cuisine or soba for lunch; grilled skewers or family-friendly diner for dinner.
- **Local transport:** **¥2,500–¥4,000** total, depending on train/bus use and optional taxi.
- **Meal budget:** **¥10,000–¥14,000** total.

Action: [Button: Arashiyama Guide] https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e3950.html

### Day 4: Northern Kyoto and Family Finish
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/water.svg
- **Morning:** Kinkaku-ji to see the Golden Pavilion.
- **Afternoon:** Ryoan-ji or Ninna-ji for a quieter temple visit, then finish with a relaxed café stop.
- **Kid-friendly activity:** A calm temple garden visit plus a dessert stop to end the trip.
- **Food:** Simple lunch near the temple area; final dinner in central Kyoto with a broader menu for everyone.
- **Local transport:** **¥2,000–¥3,500** total.
- **Meal budget:** **¥9,000–¥12,000** total.

Action: [Button: Kinkaku-ji Info] https://www.shokoku-ji.jp/kinkakuji/

## Budget Breakdown and Packing Checklist

| Category | Estimated Total | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Lodging | $620–$900 | 3–4 nights in a family-friendly hotel or apartment |
| Local transport | $35–$65 | Trains, buses, occasional taxi |
| Meals | $250–$380 | Mix of casual restaurants, market snacks, and café stops |
| Entrance fees | $40–$90 | Temples, gardens, and one optional kid activity |
| Snacks and extras | $80–$150 | Drinks, desserts, souvenirs |
| Buffer | $150–$250 | Weather, taxi, or spontaneous purchases |
| Total | **$1,175–$1,835** | Stays near your **$1,800** cap with moderate lodging |

### Spring Packing Checklist
- Light jacket or cardigan for cool mornings and evenings
- Comfortable walking shoes
- Compact umbrella or rain shell
- Layered clothing: long-sleeve tops, T-shirts, and one warmer layer
- Small daypack for water, snacks, and wipes
- Portable charger
- Child essentials: snacks, tissues, hand sanitizer, and a small entertainment item for transit
- Socks that are easy to remove for temple visits
- Reusable water bottle
